mainTopic: Hidden sins of צדיקים and related aggadot, then throwing across domains on שבת: קלוטה כמה שהונחה, the height zones, and the source of לבוד
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה בן בתירא about revealing sins the Torah keeps hidden. רבי יהודה בן בתירא never received the גזירה שוה that makes צלפחד the מקושש, so for him צלפחד was one of the מעפילים. They argue the same way about whether אהרן also got צרעת, and a ברייתא supports רבי עקיבא. Several aggadic teachings follow. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ says one who suspects innocent people is struck in his body, as משה was. Good from ה׳ comes faster than punishment. אהרן's staff swallowing the other staffs was a miracle within a miracle. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about throwing from one רשות היחיד to another through רשות הרבים. It proves that רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue below ten טפחים about קלוטה כמה שהונחה. It then brings other views on the height zones and shows that לבוד is a הלכה למשה מסיני. The amud ends with רבי's view on throwing across a roofed private domain, and רב חנא begins to raise a difficulty that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Didn't רבי עקיבא have a source for identifying צלפחד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה בן בתירא: רבי עקיבא did not invent his claim, because he learned it from a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי עקיבא learned it from a verbal analogy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יהודה בן בתירא's complaint against רבי עקיבא. It points out that רבי עקיבא had a real Torah source for saying צלפחד was the מקושש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירא said, 'The Torah hid it, and you reveal it!' A גזירה שוה is itself part of the Torah's teaching, so the Torah did not really hide the information. It revealed it through this method.

keyTerms.meaning: Verbal analogy: linking two verses through a shared word

steps.confusionAlert: This question is aimed at רבי יהודה בן בתירא, not at רבי עקיבא. The גמרא is asking how רבי יהודה בן בתירא could object when רבי עקיבא had a source.

phrases.english: But didn't he (Rabbi Akiva) learn it from a verbal analogy?!
phrases.notes: The analogy links the word 'in the wilderness' (במדבר) in the story of the מקושש and in the words of צלפחד's daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier part of the daf, where רבי יהודה בן בתירא objected to רבי עקיבא's identification of the מקושש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בן בתירא's claim that רבי עקיבא revealed what the Torah concealed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Information derived from a גזירה שוה counts as revealed by the Torah, so the objection seems baseless.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא did not receive that גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה בן בתירא never received this גזירה שוה from his teachers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not learn the verbal analogy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה בן בתירא. He had no tradition of this גזירה שוה, so in his view רבי עקיבא's claim had no source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot make up a גזירה שוה on his own. It must come through a tradition from his teachers. Without that tradition, רבי יהודה בן בתירא saw רבי עקיבא's statement as exposing a hidden sin with no basis.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule: a גזירה שוה depends on a received tradition. It is not something a person can invent by his own reasoning.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira) did not learn the verbal analogy.
phrases.notes: He had no tradition of it from his teachers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denial of the source's validity for this opinion: the speaker never received the tradition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה בן בתירא must also accept the גזירה שוה, so his objection fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה בן בתירא lacked the tradition, so for him רבי עקיבא's claim was unsupported.

steps.title: Then what sin did צלפחד commit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רבי יהודה בן בתירא, which group was צלפחד part of?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, from where was he?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. The daughters of צלפחד said their father 'died in his own sin' (חטא), so the גמרא asks which sin that was according to רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבי יהודה בן בתירא rejects the identification with the מקושש, a gap remains. The verse still says צלפחד died because of some sin, and the גמרא wants to know which one.

phrases.english: But then, from where (which group) was he?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer in step 2 by asking what רבי יהודה בן בתירא holds instead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יהודה בן בתירא, what was צלפחד's sin?

steps.title: צלפחד was one of the מעפילים
steps.stepSummary: The answer: צלפחד was among the מעפילים, who tried to go up the mountain against ה׳'s will after the sin of the spies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was from the group of 'they presumed to go up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that צלפחד was one of the מעפילים. They tried to go up to ארץ ישראל after ה׳ said not to, and they were killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives רבי יהודה בן בתירא a sin for צלפחד without linking him to חילול שבת. The daughters' words 'he died in his own sin' are satisfied either way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They presumed (to go up)', the verse about the מַעְפִּילִים (במדבר יד:מד)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: צלפחד was the מקושש, based on a גזירה שוה. רבי יהודה בן בתירא did not receive that גזירה שוה, so for him צלפחד was one of the מעפילים.

phrases.english: He was from (those of) 'And they presumed [to go up].'
phrases.notes: This refers to the people who tried to go up the mountain after the sin of the spies (במדבר 14:44).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צלפחד was one of the מעפילים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: אהרן was also struck with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: A parallel case: רבי עקיבא learns from the word ״בם״ that אהרן was struck with צרעת along with מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a similar way, you say: 'And ה׳'s anger burned against them, and He left.' This teaches that אהרן too became leprous. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, similar case where רבי עקיבא reveals something the Torah does not say openly. He teaches that אהרן also got צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says ה׳ was angry 'with them' (״בם״, plural). It says this about both אהרן and מרים, although only מרים's צרעת is described. רבי עקיבא reads the plural to mean that the punishment, צרעת, hit both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to this matter / in a like case

phrases.english: Similar to this matter, you say:
'And the anger of ה׳ burned against them, and He left' (Numbers 12:9).
phrases.notes: 'Them' refers to both אהרן and מרים.

phrases.english: This teaches that Aaron too became leprous,
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel case with the same pattern as the צלפחד dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אהרן was also struck with צרעת, learned from the plural ״בם״.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: either way you will be held accountable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא objects with the same two-sided argument: if רבי עקיבא is right, he exposed what the Torah hid; if he is wrong, he slandered a צדיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא said to him: עקיבא, either way you will have to give a judgment. If it is as you say, the Torah covered it up and you reveal it? And if not, you spread slander about that righteous man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן בתירא challenges רבי עקיבא's statement about אהרן. He traps him from both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the claim is true, the Torah chose to stay silent about אהרן's punishment, and revealing it goes against the Torah's choice. If the claim is false, it is plain slander against אהרן. Either way, רבי עקיבא should not say it.

keyTerms.meaning: To give a judgment (be held accountable in Heaven)

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a value in learning: we must be very careful before attributing sins or punishments to צדיקים that the Torah does not openly state.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira said to him:
Akiva, either way,
you will in the future have to give a judgment (be held accountable).
If it is as you say,
the Torah concealed him (his punishment), and you reveal it?!
And if not,

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה מוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק.
phrases.english: you are spreading slander about that righteous man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's teaching in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's claim that אהרן was struck with צרעת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided trap: true means exposing what the Torah hid, false means slander. Both outcomes are wrong.

steps.title: But the verse says 'them'!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה בן בתירא: the verse itself says ״בם״, so the Torah did hint at אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'against them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה בן בתירא again, just as in step 1. The plural word ״בם״ seems to be a real source that includes אהרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah wrote 'them', it seems the Torah itself told us אהרן was punished too. So רבי עקיבא was not exposing a hidden matter.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written (introduces a verse used as a challenge)

phrases.english: But it is written 'against them'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה בן בתירא's objection in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בן בתירא's claim that the Torah concealed אהרן's punishment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural ״בם״ explicitly includes אהרן in ה׳'s anger.

steps.title: אהרן received only a rebuke
steps.stepSummary: The answer: for אהרן‎, ה׳'s anger was only a rebuke, not צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was merely a rebuke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה בן בתירא. ״בם״ does include אהרן, but only in ה׳'s anger and scolding, not in the צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being included in ה׳'s anger does not mean being included in the punishment. אהרן was scolded, and only מרים was struck. So the verse gives no proof that אהרן got צרעת.

phrases.english: That (anger) was merely with a rebuke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בם″ means both received ה׳'s anger, but for אהרן it was only a rebuke.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי עקיבא: אהרן 'turned' from his צרעת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי עקיבא. It reads 'and אהרן turned' as 'he turned away from (was healed of) his צרעת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא according to the one who says אהרן too became leprous, as it is written: 'And אהרן turned to מרים, and behold she was leprous.' It was taught: this means he turned (was healed) from his leprosy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבי עקיבא that אהרן also got צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word ״ויפן״ (turned) to mean that אהרן 'turned away' from his own צרעת and was healed. That only makes sense if he had צרעת in the first place. This supports רבי עקיבא against רבי יהודה בן בתירא's reading of 'only a rebuke'.

keyTerms.meaning: A בָּרַיְיתָא was taught in line with the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: אהרן was also struck with צרעת, from ״בם״ and supported by the ברייתא on ״ויפן״. רבי יהודה בן בתירא: אהרן only received a rebuke, and saying otherwise slanders a צדיק.

phrases.english: It was taught in a Baraisa in accordance with the one who says
that Aaron too became leprous,
as it is written: 'And Aaron turned to Miriam,
and behold, she was leprous' (Numbers 12:10),
and it was taught: that he turned (was healed) from his leprosy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אַף אַהֲרֹן נִצְטָרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי יהודה בן בתירא in step 8, the גמרא brings support for רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's opinion that אהרן was struck with צרעת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ״ויפן אהרן״ as 'he turned from his צרעת'

steps.title: ריש לקיש: suspecting the innocent brings bodily punishment
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ teaches that one who suspects innocent people is punished in his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: One who suspects worthy people is struck in his body.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the theme of צרעת as a punishment for speaking against the righteous, the גמרא brings רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's general rule. Someone who wrongly suspects good people is punished physically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרים (and according to רבי עקיבא, אהרן) were struck in their bodies for speaking against משה. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ broadens this into a rule: wrongly suspecting the innocent brings a bodily punishment.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
One who suspects worthy people is struck in his body,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הַחוֹשֵׁד בִּכְשֵׁרִים לוֹקֶה בְּגוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connected by theme to the צרעת of מרים and אהרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who wrongly suspects innocent people is punished in his body.

steps.title: The proof from משה at the burning bush
steps.stepSummary: The proof: משה said the Jewish people would not believe him, but ה׳ knew they would. ה׳ answered that they are believers, and that משה himself would end up not believing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'But they will not believe me,' etc. And it was revealed before the Holy One, Blessed be He, that the Jewish people would believe. He said to him: They are believers, children of believers, and you will ultimately not believe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's rule. משה suspected the Jewish people of not believing, though they were in fact believers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה suspected people who were innocent, since ה׳ knew they would believe. ה׳ rebuked him and said that in the end משה would be the one who does not believe. The bodily punishment itself, משה's hand turning leprous, comes in the verses right after (שמות ד:ו), which the גמרא continues to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He
In the end you will not believe

steps.confusionAlert: The bodily punishment is not written in this line. Step 13 shows it: משה's hand became leprous like snow (שמות ד:ו).

phrases.english: as it is written: 'But they will not believe me,' etc. (Exodus 4:1),
and it was revealed before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
that the Jewish people would believe.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: הֵן מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים,
phrases.english: He said to him: They are believers, children of believers,
phrases.notes: 'Children of believers' refers to אברהם, who believed in ה׳.

phrases.english: and you, in the end, will not believe.
phrases.notes: This hints at what happened at מי מריבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the verse-based proof for רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's statement in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's rule that one who suspects the innocent is punished in his body
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות ד:א: משה suspected the Jewish people, who were in fact believers (followed by his hand becoming leprous).

steps.title: The verses behind ה׳'s answer to משה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק for each part of ה׳'s answer. The people are believers, they are children of believers (אברהם אבינו), and משה himself will later fail to believe.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are believers, as it says: 'And the people believed.' They are children of believers: 'And he (אברהם) believed in ה׳.' You will end up not believing, as it says: 'Because you did not believe in Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up each part of ה׳'s reply to משה with a פסוק. This continues the proof for רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each claim gets its own source. 'Believers' comes from the people's reaction in Egypt. 'Children of believers' comes from אברהם. 'You will not believe' comes from the episode of hitting the rock (מי מריבה). This shows that משה's suspicion of the people was unjustified.

keyTerms.meaning: Children of believers, meaning descendants of אברהם אבינו
In the end you will not believe

steps.confusionAlert: The last פסוק, 'Because you did not believe in Me,' does not come from the story at the burning bush. It comes from the much later episode of the rock, in ספר במדבר‎. ה׳ is predicting משה's future.

phrases.english: They are believers,
as it is written: 'And the people believed.'
phrases.notes: שמות 4:31

phrases.english: They are children of believers —
'And he believed in ה׳.'
phrases.notes: Said about אברהם, בראשית 15:6

phrases.english: You, in the end, will not believe,
as it is said: 'Because you did not believe in Me, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 20:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוקים for the claims summarized in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: ה׳'s statement that the Jewish people are believers and that משה will fail to believe

steps.title: Proof that משה was struck in his body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that משה was punished physically. It answers from the פסוק where his hand became white with צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know he was struck? As it says: 'And ה׳ said to him further: Put your hand into your bosom...' and it came out with צרעת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's proof by showing the actual bodily punishment: משה's hand turned leprous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 10 has two parts: suspecting innocent people, and being punished in the body. The suspicion was already shown. This פסוק shows the bodily punishment, so the proof is now complete.

keyTerms.meaning: Your bosom (inside your garment, against your chest)

steps.whatToRemember: One who suspects innocent people is punished in his body. משה suspected the Jewish people, and his hand was struck with צרעת.

phrases.english: From where do we know that he was struck?
As it is written: 'And ה׳ said to him further:
Bring your hand into your bosom, etc.'
phrases.notes: שמות 4:6. The פסוק continues that his hand came out leprous like snow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof by showing the bodily punishment.
steps.raayaObject: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ's rule that one who suspects innocent people is punished in his body

steps.title: Good comes faster than punishment
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or some say רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, teaches that ה׳'s good comes more quickly than His punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: The way of goodness comes faster than the way of punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching is stated, built on the same story of משה's hand. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a general rule about how ה׳ acts. When ה׳ brings good, it arrives quickly. Punishment comes more slowly.

keyTerms.meaning: The attribute of goodness or reward

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina:
The attribute of goodness comes more quickly
than the attribute of punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוקים about משה's hand to teach a new idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s good comes faster than His punishment.

steps.title: Proof from משה's hand being healed inside his bosom
steps.stepSummary: The צרעת appeared only after משה took his hand out. The healing, though, already happened while his hand was still inside his bosom.
steps.simpleTranslation: For punishment it says: 'He took it out, and behold, his hand was leprous like snow.' For goodness it says: 'He took it out from his bosom, and behold, it had returned like his flesh.' Already in his bosom it returned to be like his flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the rule by comparing the wording of two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the punishment פסוק, the צרעת is described only after the hand is taken out. In the healing פסוק, the extra word 'מֵחֵיקוֹ' (from his bosom) shows the hand was already healed before it came out. So the good came faster.

keyTerms.meaning: Returned to be like his normal flesh

steps.whatToRemember: The extra word 'מֵחֵיקוֹ' teaches that משה's hand healed while it was still inside his bosom. Good comes faster than punishment.

phrases.english: For regarding the attribute of punishment it is written:
'And he took it out, and behold, his hand was leprous like snow,'
whereas regarding the attribute of goodness it is written:
'And he took it out from his bosom,
and behold, it had returned like his flesh' —
it was already from his bosom that it returned to be like his flesh.
phrases.notes: The healing happened before the hand came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the rule stated in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that good comes faster than punishment
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparing שמות 4:6 with שמות 4:7, focusing on the word מֵחֵיקוֹ

steps.title: אהרן's staff: a miracle within a miracle
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that אהרן's staff swallowed the staffs of the Egyptian magicians. This was a double miracle.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And אהרן's staff swallowed their staffs.' רבי אלעזר said: A miracle within a miracle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching about miracles from the same period. This one concerns אהרן's staff in front of פרעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'staff,' not 'snake.' This shows that אהרן's staff swallowed the others after it had already turned back into a staff. That made it a second miracle on top of the first.

phrases.english: 'And Aaron's staff swallowed their staffs,'
phrases.notes: שמות 7:12

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: נֵס בְּתוֹךְ נֵס.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: A miracle within a miracle.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיִּבְלַע מַטֵּה אַהֲרֹן אֶת מַטֹּתָם״, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related aggadic teaching about miracles in Egypt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אהרן's staff, not his snake, swallowed the other staffs. This was a double miracle.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: throwing from one private domain to another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה. It quotes the case of throwing an object from one רשות היחיד to another רשות היחיד, with רשות הרבים in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: From a private domain to a private domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The aggadah is finished, and the גמרא is going back to the משנה. It quotes the next case to set up a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא holds the thrower חייב, and the חכמים hold him פטור. Quoting these words opens the analysis of their dispute in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Public domain (the area in between in this case)

steps.confusionAlert: Both ends of the throw are private domains. The question is whether passing through רשות הרבים in the middle makes the thrower liable.

phrases.english: From the private domain to the private domain.
phrases.notes: Quoted from the משנה, where the object passes through a public domain in between.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the aggadic digression and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the משנה's case of throwing between two private domains through a public domain, where רבי עקיבא holds חייב and the חכמים hold פטור.

steps.title: רבה's question, first option: they argue below ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: רבה suggests that רבי עקיבא and the חכמים may argue only about an object flying below ten טפחים. On this view, the issue is קלוטה כמה שהונחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked: Maybe they argue when the object flew below ten טפחים. On this view, one side holds that a flying object counts as if it landed, and the other side holds it does not. Above ten, everyone would agree he is פטור, because we do not learn throwing from handing over.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה opens a question about the משנה's dispute. He lays out the first of two possible ways to understand it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below ten טפחים, the object is flying inside the real space of רשות הרבים. רבי עקיבא would say it is treated as if it landed there, so he is חייב. The חכמים disagree. Above ten, the air is not really רשות הרבים, so everyone says פטור, and we do not borrow the rule of מושיט for throwing.

keyTerms.meaning: Below ten טפחים (handbreadths) from the ground
An object caught in the air is treated as if it was placed down
One who hands over or passes an object by hand

steps.confusionAlert: Ten טפחים matters because רשות הרבים only goes up ten טפחים from the ground. Air above that height is not really part of רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: Rabba asked:
Do they disagree about below ten handbreadths,
and this is what they disagree about:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר אָמְרִינַן קְלוּטָה כְּמָה שֶׁהוּנְּחָה,
phrases.english: that this master holds we say an object in the air counts as placed down,
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר לָא אָמְרִינַן קְלוּטָה כְּמָה שֶׁהוּנְּחָה.
phrases.english: and this master holds we do not say an object in the air counts as placed down.
phrases.notes: חכמים

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: But above ten, everyone agrees he is exempt,
and we do not learn throwing from handing over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what exactly the dispute in the משנה quoted in step 17 is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: At what height do רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue, and what principle is behind their argument?

steps.title: רבה's question, second option: they argue above ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe they argue only above ten טפחים, and the issue is whether we learn זורק from מושיט. Below ten, everyone would say חייב because of קלוטה כמה שהונחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe they argue when the object flew above ten טפחים. On this view, one side learns throwing from handing over, and the other side does not. Below ten, everyone would agree he is חייב, because a flying object counts as if it landed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives the second side of his question. Here the dispute moves up above ten טפחים and becomes about a different principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, everyone accepts קלוטה כמה שהונחה below ten, so there is no argument there. The argument is about above ten. Handing an object across by hand is חייב even that high. The question is whether throwing works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)
Above ten טפחים from the ground
Is comparable to / is treated like

steps.whatToRemember: The two options: (1) the argument is below ten, about קלוטה כמה שהונחה; (2) the argument is above ten, about learning זורק from מושיט.

phrases.english: Or perhaps they disagree about above ten,
and this is what they disagree about:
that this master holds we learn throwing from handing over,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר לָא יָלְפִינַן זוֹרֵק מִמּוֹשִׁיט.
phrases.english: and this master holds we do not learn throwing from handing over.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְמַטָּה מֵעֲשָׂרָה — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: But below ten, everyone agrees he is liable.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא? — קְלוּטָה כְּמָה שֶׁהוּנְּחָה דָּמְיָא.
phrases.english: What is the reason? An object in the air is treated as placed down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of רבה's question from step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument actually above ten, about whether זורק is learned from מושיט?

steps.title: רב המנונא proves from a ברייתא that they argue below ten
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that רב חסדא had this same question. רב המנונא answered it from a ברייתא that says the object passes 'through רשות הרבים itself,' which means below ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב חסדא had this exact question, and רב המנונא answered it from this ברייתא. 'From רשות היחיד to רשות היחיד, passing through רשות הרבים itself: רבי עקיבא says חייב and the חכמים say פטור.' Since it says 'רשות הרבים itself,' it is clear they argue about below ten.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא begins to answer רבה's question. It brings a ברייתא whose wording points to the first option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'itself' (עצמה) tells us the object flew through the real space of רשות הרבים, which is below ten טפחים. So the argument between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים is about below ten. The גמרא still has to show which principle drives that argument, and that comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself, meaning the actual space of רשות הרבים, below ten

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא מִילְּתָא אִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Rav Chisda had a question about this very matter,
and Rav Hamnuna resolved it for him from this:
From a private domain to a private domain
and it passes through the public domain itself:
Rabbi Akiva holds him liable, and the Rabbis exempt him.
Since it says 'through the public domain itself,'
it is clear that they disagree about below ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: הָא מִילְּתָא אִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב חִסְדָּא, וּפַשְׁטַהּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא מֵהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer רבה's two-sided question from steps 18 and 19.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute is about an object traveling below ten טפחים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא whose wording says the object passes through 'רשות הרבים itself'

steps.title: The ברייתא cannot be about carrying by hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of transfer the ברייתא means. It rules out carrying by hand, because רבי אלעזר says carrying by hand is חייב even above ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is the ברייתא talking about? If you say it is about carrying by hand, would he be חייב only below ten and not above ten? But רבי אלעזר said that someone who carries a load out above ten טפחים is חייב, because that is how the בני קהת carried their load in the מדבר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks what kind of case the ברייתא is about. It rejects the idea that it means carrying by hand. This sets up the next step, which will say the ברייתא must be about throwing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא suggests that רבי עקיבא is חייב only below ten. For carrying by hand, though, height makes no difference: you are חייב even above ten. רבי אלעזר learns this from the בני קהת, who carried the משכן's vessels high on their shoulders. So the ברייתא cannot be about carrying by hand.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries something across by hand
But didn't (a sage) say? (introduces a challenge)
The load carried by the sons of קהת, the לויים who carried the משכן's vessels

phrases.english: And in what case?
If you say it is about carrying across by hand,
is it only below ten that he is liable,
and above ten he is not liable?
But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
One who carries out a load above ten is liable,
for that is how the sons of Kehat carried their load.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out what kind of transfer the ברייתא from step 20 is describing.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the ברייתא is about carrying by hand (מעביר)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Carrying by hand is חייב even above ten (רבי אלעזר, from בני קהת). So a ruling of חייב only below ten cannot be about carrying by hand.

steps.title: So it is about throwing, and the dispute is whether a flying object counts as landed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must be about throwing, where being below ten matters. So the argument between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים is about קלוטה כמה שהונחה. The גמרא agrees with this conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it about throwing? Below ten he is חייב, and above ten he is not. Learn from this that they argue about whether a flying object counts as if it landed. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is about throwing. That means the first option of רבה's question is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With throwing, height does matter, since only below ten is the object flying inside רשות הרבים. The two sides argue below ten, so the issue must be קלוטה כמה שהונחה. רבי עקיבא says a flying object counts as landed, and the חכמים say it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it? (introduces the remaining option)
Learn from it (a conclusion is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's question is answered: רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue about throwing below ten טפחים, and the issue is קלוטה כמה שהונחה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines רבי עקיבא's position as קלוטה כמה שהונחה. Later סוגיות build on that idea.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it about throwing,
and it is below ten that he is liable,
and above ten he is not liable?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ בִּקְלוּטָה כְּמָה שֶׁהוּנְּחָה פְּלִיגִי.
phrases.english: Learn from it that they disagree about whether an object in the air counts as placed down.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carrying by hand was ruled out in step 21, so the ברייתא must be about throwing, which settles רבה's question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים is about throwing below ten טפחים, over whether קלוטה כמה שהונחה applies.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר Holds רבי עקיבא Obligates Even Above Ten
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion from the previous step disagrees with רבי אלעזר. He says רבי עקיבא holds חייב even above ten טפחים. The ברייתא's phrase 'רשות הרבים itself' only comes to show how far the רבנן go.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר said: רבי עקיבא would hold a person חייב even if the object flew above ten טפחים. The ברייתא says 'רשות הרבים itself' only to show how strong the רבנן's position is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא who disagrees with the conclusion we just reached. That conclusion was that the argument is only below ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We had proven from the words 'רשות הרבים itself' that the argument is below ten. רבי אלעזר reads those words differently. They do not limit רבי עקיבא. They show that the רבנן say פטור even when the object passes right through the street itself, and all the more so above ten. So for רבי אלעזר, רבי עקיבא holds חייב at any height.

keyTerms.meaning: And this disagrees with (another אמורא's view)
Above ten טפחים, where the space is no longer counted as רשות הרבים
To show you how far their position goes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 21. There, רבי אלעזר's ruling was about carrying a load out by hand (המוציא משוי, the מעביר case), learned from the בני קהת. Here he is talking about רבי עקיבא's view on throwing. He holds that רבי עקיבא obligates the thrower even above ten.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Elazar.
For Rabbi Elazar said:
Rabbi Akiva would hold him liable
even above ten handbreadths,
and the fact that it teaches 'the public domain itself' —
phrases.notes: The same ברייתא wording used as proof in step 20

phrases.english: is to show you the strength of the Rabbis' view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an אמורא who reads the ברייתא from step 20 differently and so disagrees with the conclusion of step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, רבי עקיבא holds חייב even when the thrown object flew above ten טפחים. The phrase 'רשות הרבים itself' only highlights how strong the רבנן's פטור is.

steps.title: רב חלקיה בר טובי's Three Height Zones
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר's view clashes with רב חלקיה בר טובי. He says: below three טפחים, everyone holds חייב. Above ten, everyone holds פטור. Between three and ten is where רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רב חלקיה בר טובי. רב חלקיה בר טובי said: within three טפחים of the ground, everyone agrees he is חייב. Above ten, everyone agrees he is פטור. From three up to ten is the argument between רבי עקיבא and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that another אמורא disagrees with רבי אלעזר. This אמורא gives a clear map of heights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below three, the object counts as if it is lying on the ground because of the rule of לבוד, so everyone holds חייב. Above ten is outside רשות הרבים, so everyone holds פטור, which directly contradicts רבי אלעזר. The only real argument about קלוטה כמה שהונחה is in the middle zone, between three and ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Within three טפחים of the ground
The rule that anything within three טפחים of a surface is treated as attached to it
From three up to ten טפחים

steps.whyThisMatters: This three-zone map makes the argument between רבי עקיבא and the רבנן much narrower than it first looked. It only applies between three and ten טפחים.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Chilkiya bar Tovi,
for Rav Chilkiya bar Tovi said:
Within three handbreadths — everyone agrees he is liable.
phrases.notes: Because of לבוד, the object counts as resting on the ground.

phrases.english: Above ten — everyone agrees he is exempt.
From three until ten —
we come to the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי אלעזר's view from step 23 conflicts with another אמורא, who says everyone holds פטור above ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Below three טפחים, everyone holds חייב. Above ten, everyone holds פטור. Between three and ten, רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue.

steps.title: A ברייתא Supports רב חלקיה בר טובי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same three zones as רב חלקיה בר טובי. It adds that above ten, the only problem is a rabbinic שבות, and if both private domains belong to the same person, it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this. Within three טפחים, everyone agrees he is חייב. Above ten, it is only forbidden because of a rabbinic שבות, and if both domains are his, it is permitted. From three to ten, רבי עקיבא holds חייב and the חכמים hold פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב חלקיה בר טובי said. This supports his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms the three zones. It adds a detail about throwing above ten from one private domain to another: there is no Torah prohibition, only a rabbinic one. That rabbinic prohibition applies to domains owned by different people without an עירוב. If the same person owns both domains, there is no problem at all.
steps.whatToRemember: Below three: everyone holds חייב. Between three and ten: the argument. Above ten: only a rabbinic שבות, and permitted if both domains are his.

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:
Within three handbreadths — everyone agrees he is liable;

phrases.aramaic: לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה — אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת.
phrases.english: above ten — it is forbidden only because of a rabbinic decree.
And if both domains were his — it is permitted.
phrases.notes: The next step will build its challenge on this line.

phrases.english: From three until ten —
Rabbi Akiva holds liable and the Sages exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חלקיה בר טובי's three zones from step 24 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חלקיה בר טובי's three height zones
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists the same three zones and adds the rule about domains owned by one person

steps.title: Does the ברייתא Refute רב on Throwing Between Two Houses?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא permits throwing above ten between two domains owned by one person. This seems to refute רב, who forbids throwing between two houses on opposite sides of רשות הרבים. שמואל permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'If both domains are his, it is permitted.' Shall we say this refutes רב? For it was stated: about two houses on two sides of רשות הרבים, רבה בר רב הונא said in the name of רב that it is forbidden to throw from one to the other. And שמואל said it is permitted to throw from one to the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes one line from the ברייתא and uses it to challenge רב. רב forbade something this ברייתא seems to permit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב forbids throwing between two houses across רשות הרבים, even when one person owns both. The ברייתא says that when both domains belong to one person, throwing above ten is permitted. So the ברייתא seems to contradict רב and support שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this is a refutation of
To throw from this one to that one

phrases.english: The Master said:
If both domains were his — it is permitted.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes this line from the ברייתא again so it can look at it closely.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav,
for it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי בָתִּים בִּשְׁנֵי צִדֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: Two houses on two sides of the public domain,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
It is forbidden to throw from this one to that one.
And Shmuel said:
It is permitted to throw from this one to that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the extra rule from the ברייתא in step 25 to challenge רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one may not throw between two houses on opposite sides of רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits throwing above ten between two domains owned by one person. רב forbids exactly this kind of throw, so the ברייתא seems to contradict him.

steps.title: רב Was Talking About One High House and One Low House
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is answered. רב's ruling was already explained as a case where one house is higher than the other. There, the object may fall into the street, and the person may go bring it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we already explain that ruling as a case where one house is high and one is low? Sometimes the object falls, and he will come to bring it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. It reminds us that his ruling was already limited to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the two houses are at different heights, the throw is harder and the object can easily drop into רשות הרבים. The person might then carry it back, which would break a Torah prohibition. So רב's ban is a safeguard for that specific case. It does not argue with the ברייתא, which is talking about a normal throw.

keyTerms.meaning: We established (limited a ruling to a specific case)
One is high and one is low
He will come to bring it back

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ban on throwing between two houses only applies when one house is higher than the other. The worry is that the object will fall and the person will carry it back from רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: But didn't we establish that ruling
as a case where one is high and one is low —
for sometimes it falls,
and he will come to bring it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב from step 26 by limiting his ruling to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב forbids all throwing between two houses, which would contradict the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב only forbids throwing when one house is higher than the other, because the object might fall and be carried back. So he does not contradict the ברייתא.

steps.title: Where does the rule of לבוד come from?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב המנונא discuss the source for the rule that a gap of less than three טפחים counts as closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רב המנונא (some say רב המנונא said to רב חסדא): Where do we learn the rule the רבנן said, that anything less than three טפחים is treated as לבוד, as if it were joined together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks for the source or reason behind the well-known rule of לבוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of לבוד was just used in the sugya: under three טפחים counts as resting on the ground. Now the גמרא wants to know why this is true. Is it based on logic, or is it a tradition?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Joined': a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as if it were closed
'From where is this matter?' A request for a source

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rav Hamnuna,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Hamnuna said to Rav Chisda:
phrases.notes: Two versions of who asked whom.

phrases.english: From where is this matter that the Rabbis said:
Anything less than three is considered lavud (joined)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a side discussion about the לבוד rule that the earlier sugya relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reason for the rule of לבוד.

steps.title: A logical reason: the street can never be perfectly level
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a public street can never be smoothed perfectly flat, so small bumps under three טפחים count as part of the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: Because a רשות הרבים can never be made perfectly flat with smoothing tools and planes.
steps.whatsHappening: An answer is given. It offers a common-sense reason for the rule of לבוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ground in a public area always has bumps and dips. So something resting slightly above the ground is still treated as lying on the ground. This makes לבוד a matter of logic, not a tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: A tool for leveling or smoothing ground
Planes, tools for smoothing a surface

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
phrases.english: Because it is impossible for the public domain
to be leveled with a leveler and with planes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָהּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לבוד is based on logic: the uneven ground of a רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Then why not exactly three as well?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is uneven ground, why does the rule stop just under three? Three should count too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then a gap of exactly three should also count as joined!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the logical reason. A loose idea like 'the ground is bumpy' does not explain such an exact cut-off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bumpy ground could be off by three טפחים just as easily as by less than three. A logical reason should not create a sharp line exactly at three. So the reason does not match the precise rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so': if your reason is correct

phrases.english: If so, three also?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The logical reason of uneven ground.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rough reason based on bumpy ground cannot produce an exact limit of 'less than three'.

steps.title: לבוד also works in a סוכה, far from any street
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: the משנה about סוכה walls uses the same 'under three' rule, where the street's bumps have nothing to do with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, we learned in a משנה: If someone lets the walls of a סוכה hang down from the top, and they are three טפחים above the ground, the סוכה is פסולה. This implies that if they are less than three above the ground, it is כשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge. It brings a משנה about a סוכה where the 'under three' rule also applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוכה has nothing to do with a bumpy public street. Still, a gap under three below the wall counts as closed. So the street-based reason cannot be the real source of לבוד.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lowers walls downward from above

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which we learned:
One who lowers walls from top to bottom,

phrases.aramaic: אִם הֵן גְּבוֹהִין מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים — פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: if they are three handbreadths above the ground, it is invalid.
Implying: less than three, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on the reason given in step 29.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לבוד applies in a סוכה, where uneven public ground is not a factor.

steps.title: In a סוכה the reason is goats getting through
steps.stepSummary: Defense: in the סוכה case the reason is different. A gap of three lets young goats slip under, so it is no real wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the reason is that it would be a wall that young goats can get through.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the סוכה challenge. The סוכה rule has its own reason, so it does not disprove the street reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wall with a gap of three or more lets small goats pass under it, so it does not work as a wall. Under three, the goats cannot get through. So the סוכה rule is not based on לבוד at all.

phrases.english: There, this is the reason:
because it would be
a partition that young goats pass through.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the סוכה challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason for the cited case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוכה case shows לבוד applies outside the street.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סוכה case is based on goats passing through, not on לבוד.

steps.title: Goats explain gaps near the ground, not gaps up high
steps.stepSummary: The goat reason works for a gap at the bottom, but לבוד also applies to gaps up high, where goats are irrelevant.
steps.simpleTranslation: That works for a gap below. But for a gap above, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the goat answer. It shows that the answer only covers some cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goats can only slip through a gap near the ground. But לבוד also applies up high, such as a gap near the roof of a סוכה. Neither the street reason nor the goat reason explains that.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works out well': fine for this case
'What is there to say?' There is no good answer

phrases.english: It works out fine below;
above, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח לְמַטָּה, לְמַעְלָה מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the goat answer of step 32.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לבוד applies to gaps up high, where goats cannot pass, so goats cannot be the reason.

steps.title: לבוד is a tradition from סיני
steps.stepSummary: Conclusion: the rule of לבוד has no logical source. It is a הלכה למשה מסיני, learned by tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the rule that anything less than three is considered לבוד is a הלכה that was learned by tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on finding a logical reason. It concludes that לבוד is a received tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every logical reason failed to explain the exact limit and all the cases. A הלכה למשה מסיני can have an exact measure and apply everywhere. That fits how לבוד works.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We learned it as a הלכה': a הלכה למשה מסיני passed down by tradition

steps.whatToRemember: לבוד (a gap under three טפחים counts as closed) is a הלכה למשה מסיני. It is not based on bumpy ground or goats, which is why it has an exact limit and applies both high and low.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the goat reason is the source of לבוד. It explained only the סוכה case near the ground, and the גמרא set it aside as the source.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because לבוד is a tradition, it applies in every area of הלכה (שבת, סוכה, and more), not only in a רשות הרבים.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כׇּל פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה כְּלָבוּד דָּמֵי —
phrases.english: Rather, anything less than three is considered lavud —
it is a halacha learned by tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כׇּל פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה כְּלָבוּד דָּמֵי הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question of step 28 after the reasons failed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: לבוד is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Throwing between two public domains across a private one
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: throwing from one רשות הרבים to another, with a רשות היחיד in between. רבי says חייב, the חכמים say פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If someone throws from a רשות הרבים to a רשות הרבים, with a רשות היחיד in the middle, רבי holds him חייב and the חכמים hold him פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It is a case like the one in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The object flies through the air of the רשות היחיד but never lands there. רבי still holds the thrower חייב for its passing through, and the חכמים exempt him because it never landed. The next step, from רב and שמואל, explains the reason for רבי's view and limits it: a roofed house counts as 'full'.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From a public domain to a public domain
with a private domain in the middle —
Rabbi holds liable, and the Sages exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic related to the משנה's throwing cases.

steps.title: רבי holds him חייב only if the private domain has a roof
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל limit רבי's view to a roofed רשות היחיד, which is seen as 'full'. If there is no roof, even רבי says פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both said: רבי only holds him חייב when the רשות היחיד has a roof, because we say a house is treated as if it were full. But if it has no roof, he is not חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל explain the ברייתא. They narrow רבי's ruling to one kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A roofed house is treated as if it were filled up, so the flying object counts as landing inside. An open yard has no such rule. So even רבי agrees there is no liability there.

keyTerms.meaning: A house is treated as if it were full

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel both said:
Rabbi held liable only
in a covered private domain,
since we say a house is considered as if it were full,
but one that is not covered, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: לֹא חִיֵּיב רַבִּי אֶלָּא בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד מְקוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי's ruling from step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי holds him חייב only when the רשות היחיד is roofed.

steps.title: רבי would require two קרבנות
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says רבי holds him חייב two קרבנות חטאת: one for bringing the object into the private domain, and one for taking it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא said in the name of רב יהודה, who said it in the name of שמואל: רבי would hold him חייב two: one for הוצאה (taking out) and one for הכנסה (bringing in).
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds how far רבי's ruling goes. One throw creates two separate violations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The object enters the רשות היחיד from the first public area. That is bringing in. Then it leaves into the second public area. That is taking out. Since each counts as its own act, he brings two קרבנות חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking out from a private domain to a public one
Bringing in from a public domain to a private one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי holds him חייב only for a roofed private domain, which is seen as 'full'. In that case he is חייב twice: once for bringing in and once for taking out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chana said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi would hold him liable for two —
one for carrying out,
and one for carrying in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the extent of רבי's liability to the case limited in step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי, the thrower brings two קרבנות חטאת, for הכנסה and for הוצאה.

steps.title: רב חנא sits and is bothered by a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רב חנא, who was sitting and found something difficult. The actual difficulty comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא was sitting, and something was difficult for him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us that רב חנא had a question, and it is preparing us for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new about the הלכה is said here yet. The line signals that what follows is a challenge. It comes right after שמואל's ruling that רבי makes the thrower bring two קרבנות חטאת, so we should expect the difficulty to touch on that ruling. The exact problem is spelled out in the following line.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting. A common way the גמרא opens a story of a חכם thinking something over.
It was difficult for him. It signals that a question or challenge is about to be presented.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the actual question in this line. It only announces that a difficulty is coming. The content of the difficulty is in the next line.

phrases.english: Rav Chana was sitting
and it was difficult for him:

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב חָנָא וְקָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a challenge that comes right after שמואל's statement that רבי obligates two קרבנות חטאת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The difficulty comes right after שמואל's ruling in step 37, but its exact content is spelled out in the next line.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. This line only announces that a difficulty is coming. The actual challenge is in the following line.
